Findings:  Small knee joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Large multiloculated ganglion cyst possibly originating from the lateral head of gastrocnemius tendon origin, and extending posterosuperiorly into the surrounding soft tissues extending from the origin of the lateral head of gastrocnemius  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Radial tear of the anterior horn/body junction of the medial meniscus with partial extrusion of the body from the joint space. Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, popliteus tendon and pes anserine tendons.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons.  Severe patellofemoral degenerative change with diffuse full-thickness chondral loss along the retropatellar facets and corresponding femoral trochlea, and chronic underlying bone stress changes together with attrition/moulding of the retropatellar facets.  Full-thickness chondral loss is also appreciated in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Scattered intraosseous ganglion cyst noted in both the distal femur and proximal tibia. Tricompartmental marginal osteophyte formation also noted.  
Conclusion:  Radial tear of the body of the medial meniscus. Severe patellofemoral and to a lesser extent medial tibiofemoral compartment degenerative changes. Ancillary findings described above.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Six-week history of knee pain associated with hockey localized to the anterior knee. No prior surgery.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Mild to moderate osteoarthritis of the proximal tibiofibular joint characterized by marginal osteophyte formation, chondrosis and mild subchondral bone marrow edema.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. There is a new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body localized posterior to the PCL (series 4, image 12). No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss about the central and posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle with superimposed areas of full-thickness fissuring and mild subchondral marrow edema, progressed from prior.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness fissuring involving the median ridge and lateral patellar facet with mild subchondral marrow edema and cystic change, low-grade partial-thickness loss along the medial patellar facet peripherally. Focal full-thickness fissuring involving the mid to inferior lateral femoral trochlea with mild subchondral marrow edema superimposed on diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral femoral trochlea. [REDACTED].

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Progressive patellofemoral greater than medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2.	Small joint effusion with new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body posterior to the PCL.
3.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear.
4.	Moderate prepatellar bursitis.
